newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen says ASEAN has role in Cambodia stability.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen says ASEAN has role in Cambodia stability.

text.p: Cambodia's Hun Sen said on Thursday the Association of South East Asian Nations could play a role in ensuring Cambodia's stability and he was not upset by the group's decision to delay Cambodia's membership.
"I don't feel any upset because of that... we have to respect the decision made by ASEAN," Hun Sen told reporters.
He said Cambodia could wait for membership of ASEAN.
"We're waiting for ASEAN's decision next time," he said.
ASEAN, which already grouped Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, on Wednesday admitted Burma and Laos but delayed Cambodia's entry indefinitely.

Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot arrived in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday to attend ASEAN's annual foreign ministers' meeting as an observer and said Hun Sen had adopted a new position on ASEAN mediation efforts in Cambodia's political troubles.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6, rejected a mediation push by an ASEAN mission at the weekend, saying foreigners should keep out of Cambodia's affairs, but on Thursday Hun Sen said ASEAN's role in ensuring stability in Cambodia was needed.
"The stability of Cambodia -- we need the role of ASEAN," he said.
Diplomats from the region welcomed Hun Sen's new position on ASEAN's role in Cambodia.
"That's a very positive comment, a real departure from what he said during and after the crisis," said one Asian diplomat. "He could have said it earlier and things would have been a lot better."
"It's very good. He's sounding like a statesman," said another diplomat.
ASEAN was preparing fresh proposals for Hun Sen on Thursday in an attempt to mediate in the conflict in Cambodia, officials in Kuala Lumpur said.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who has been involved in brokering Cambodian diplomacy for years, said he and two other ASEAN ministers discussed the ideas with Ung Huot on Wednesday.
In Los Angeles on Wednesday, U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright pledged that the United States would do all it could to see that Hun Sen made good on promises to accept mediation.
A U.S. special envoy on Cambodia on Thursday applauded Hun Sen's decision to allow ASEAN a role.

"We are encouraged by what now appears to be a willingness on the part of Hun Sen to accept the ASEAN offer to use its good offices to facilitate a political resolution of the Cambodian crisis," former U.S. congressman Stephen Solarz told reporters in Bangkok after meeting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
Solarz, who is on a tour of Asian capitals seeking a solution to the turmoil in Cambodia, was due in Phnom Penh later on Thursday and was scheduled to meet Hun Sen on Friday morning.
Solarz said the United States hoped to work closely with ASEAN to try and find a solution to the problem.
